title: Sniffing

objectives.text: Explain why a switch limits what a sniffer sees, and tell passive sniffing on a hub from active sniffing on a switch
Compare SPAN port mirroring and network TAPs as legitimate capture points, and name the clear-text protocols that expose credentials
Recognize MAC flooding, DHCP starvation, rogue DHCP, ARP poisoning, MAC spoofing and DNS poisoning from a short description, log line or packet pattern
Tell Wireshark display filters from capture (BPF) filters and write simple examples of each
Read a tcpdump or Wireshark output line (ARP who-has / is-at, TCP flags, duplicate IP warning) and say what it shows
Match each attack class to the switch or network defence that stops it: port security, DHCP snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection, IP Source Guard, 802.1X, DNSSEC and encryption
Describe how defenders detect a sniffer or an ARP poisoning attempt (promiscuous-mode checks, arpwatch, IDS, Wireshark Expert Information)

readingMap.why: Know hub vs switch, promiscuous vs monitor mode, SPAN vs TAP and which protocols are clear text.
Most questions describe a layer-2 attack by its symptom and ask for its name or the feature that stops it.
Filter syntax (display vs capture) and reading an output line are tested directly.
Matching attack to defence (port security, DHCP snooping, DAI, IPSG, 802.1X, DNSSEC, encryption) is the core of the module.

labs.name: Wireshark filter practice on public sample captures
labs.skill: Opening published capture files and applying display filters such as arp, dhcp, dns and ip.addr to find each protocol

labs.name: Capture your own traffic with tcpdump
labs.skill: Capturing on your own machine with a capture filter, writing to a file with -w and reading it back with -r and -e

labs.name: Watch ARP pairings on your home lab with arpwatch
labs.skill: Running arpwatch on a lab network you own and reading its new station / changed ethernet address / flip flop reports

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a new colleague why plugging a laptop into a switch port does not let it read everyone's traffic, while a hub or an open Wi-Fi channel would.
Pick one layer-2 attack (MAC flooding, rogue DHCP or ARP poisoning) and explain what lie it tells to which device, what a defender would see in the logs, and which switch feature stops it.
Explain the difference between a Wireshark display filter and a capture filter, and why choosing the wrong one can lose evidence.
